scope: Theorem 10.2 (An input-dependent entry chart) of the manuscript “Incompressible Box Transport and Finite Computation” (preprints/Incompressible-Box-Transport-and-Finite-Computation-October-6-2026/manuscript.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 376 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 2505dc09d3f2c24b), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 35. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For each machine and finite input, and each fixed positive computable viscosity ν, there is an effective smooth force on R3 with one compact spatial support, bounded mixed derivatives, and period one from time zero, whose zero-data solution satisfies ∃t ≥ 0 : X1(t; (2, 0, 0)) < 0 ⇐⇒ the machine halts. The solution is smooth with pressure zero and is unique among smooth solutions for which, on every finite interval, u ∈ CtH2 ∩ C1 t L2, u and ∇u are bounded, and p ∈ CtH1. As a separate force choice, the same event is realized with every mixed derivative of velocity and force in space-time L2 and bounded by a derivative-dependent multiple of (1 + t)−1.
